setup.subtitle: Find the place that keeps sunlight for power and Earth in view for radio contact during your stay.
setup.textures: 3D view textures: Solar System Scope, based on NASA imagery. We resized them, added the clouds to Earth's day and night maps, and cut a patch of highlands from the Moon map to tile the ground.

timeline.legend: Bar: in view. Gap: hidden. Frame: your stay.
timeline.summary_one: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} time during this time span.
timeline.summary_other: {{lane}}: in view {{count}} times during this time span.

playback.title: Time on the Moon
playback.hint: Press Play or drag the slider to move time. The map, sky and timelines show that moment. The shaded part is your stay.
playback.keys: An arrow key moves the time 1 hour. Shift and an arrow key move it 1 day.

credits.title: Data sources
credits.positions: Sun and Earth positions: astronomy-engine. We checked them against NASA JPL Horizons. The difference is less than 0.01°.
credits.hills: Hills: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA polar height maps (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, PDS Geosciences Node). The tool looks from 2 metres above the ground.
credits.checks: We checked the hills against PGDA 69 (Mazarico et al. 2011, average sunlight at the poles). Reference height map: PGDA 90 (Barker et al. 2023).
credits.textures: 3D view textures: Solar System Scope, based on NASA imagery. We resized them, added the clouds to Earth's day and night maps, and cut a patch of highlands from the Moon map to tile the ground.

map.label: Map of the Moon's south pole with a marker for each place shown
map.labelEmpty: Map of the Moon's south pole. No places to show yet.
map.image: The ground at the Moon's south pole, drawn with shading
map.lowerBound: Our height map ends before the hills around this place end. The Sun and Earth may be hidden more often than the map shows.
map.offMap: {{site}} is too far from the pole to show on this map.
map.credit: Ground: NASA LRO LOLA height map, drawn with shading.

rank.pending: Comparing every south-pole place for your landing date and stay…
rank.failed: The tool could not compare the places, so there is no best option. Reload the page to try again.

why.only: The only place the tool could compare
why.closest: No place fits. This one is the closest.
why.onlyFit: The only one of {{count}} places that fits
why.dark: Shortest time with no Sun and no Earth, of {{count}} places
why.sunlight: Most sunlight among the best of {{count}} places
why.earth: Most time with Earth in view among the best of {{count}} places
why.tie: First of {{count}} places, equal with the next place
why.rules: The tool compares {{count}} south-pole places for your landing date and stay. A place that fits your stay comes first. Next, the tool prefers the shortest time with no Sun and no Earth. Then it prefers the most sunlight, then the most time with Earth in view.
why.leftOut: The tool does not compare {{site}}. Our height map ends before its hills end, so its numbers are upper limits only.
